title: Reconciliation Health — declared vs actual
description: Every GitOps/operator-managed resource in the cluster, split by the distinction that matters: NEVER reconciled (never worked, often an unbacked hand-made object) vs REGRESSED (worked, then broke). Built after a 7-week silent ExternalSecret failure and a 100-minute outage.

panels.title: Declared vs actual — is anything unreconciled?
NEVER reconciled
panels.description: Resources whose Ready condition has NOT been true at any point in the last 7 days. Nobody ever finished wiring these. If a hand-made object of the same name already exists, GitOps believes it is managed when it is not — that is how boomtime-encryption-key ended up as the cluster's ONLY copy of an encryption key for 7 weeks.

targets.expr:
count(
label_replace(max by (exported_namespace, name) (gotk_reconcile_condition{type="Ready", status="False"} == 1) unless on (exported_namespace, name) (max by (exported_namespace, name) (max_over_time(gotk_reconcile_condition{type="Ready", status="True"}[7d])) == 1), "source", "Flux", "", "")
  or
label_replace(max by (exported_namespace, name) (externalsecret_status_condition{condition="Ready", status="False"} == 1) unless on (exported_namespace, name) (max by (exported_namespace, name) (max_over_time(externalsecret_status_condition{condition="Ready", status="True"}[7d])) == 1), "source", "ExternalSecret", "", "")
  or
label_replace(max by (exported_namespace, name) (certmanager_certificate_ready_status{condition="False"} == 1) unless on (exported_namespace, name) (max by (exported_namespace, name) (max_over_time(certmanager_certificate_ready_status{condition="True"}[7d])) == 1), "source", "Certificate", "", "")
  or
label_replace(max by (namespace, name) (certmanager_clusterissuer_ready_status{condition="False"} == 1) unless on (namespace, name) (max by (namespace, name) (max_over_time(certmanager_clusterissuer_ready_status{condition="True"}[7d])) == 1), "source", "ClusterIssuer", "", "")
) or vector(0)

panels.title: Regressed
panels.description: Was Ready within the last 7 days and is not now. Something that worked, broke. Usually a real incident, but recoverable — the previous good state existed.

panels.title: ArgoCD orphans (in cluster, not declared)
panels.description: Live objects inside an ArgoCD Application's scope that no manifest declares. The inverse failure: declared-but-absent is above, this is present-but-undeclared. Only covers ArgoCD-managed namespaces — Flux has no equivalent orphan metric, so this is a floor, not a total.

panels.title: Reconcilers healthy
panels.description: Denominator: everything currently reconciling cleanly across Flux, ESO and cert-manager.

targets.expr: count(gotk_reconcile_condition{type="Ready", status="True"} == 1) + (count(externalsecret_status_condition{condition="Ready", status="True"} == 1) or vector(0)) + (count(certmanager_certificate_ready_status{condition="True"} == 1) or vector(0))

panels.title: NEVER reconciled — never worked since the day it was declared
Never reconciled (all sources)
panels.description: The dangerous class. For each row ask: does an object of this name already exist? `kubectl get <kind> <name> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{.metadata.ownerReferences}'` — empty ownerReferences means it was hand-made, is unbacked, and the cluster holds the only copy. Back it into the provider BEFORE anything deletes or recreates it.

panels.title: Apps not Synced / not Healthy
panels.description: ArgoCD is tracked separately because it reports two independent axes — sync_status (does the cluster match git) and health_status (is the result working). An app can be perfectly Synced and completely unhealthy.

panels.title: Unreconciled resources over time, by source
panels.description: Rising steps that never come down are the never-reconciled class — they do not self-heal and will sit here until someone acts. Spikes that recover are ordinary reconcile churn.
